sam_sales: Heads-up — Spectra asked for a final runbook + cost ballpark for their mixed thin-client workload. They want: steady 300 qps, 3k qps bursts for 30s, model=redwood-13b-quant, avg prompt ~120 tokens. SLO: p95 < 250ms for user-facing requests. Need load plan + expected tail behavior + rough $/M-token. Can eng + solutions confirm feasibility and any enterprise/security blockers?

iris_se: Ok. Quick clarifying q's: (1) Are inference requests single-turn or chat-like with 2-3 turns? (2) Any required region (NA vs multi-region)? (3) Encryption/KMS ask?

sam_sales: Single-turn for now (user prompt -> reply). NA first, potential multi-az later. Customer said they need KMS for keys but haven't sent the questionnaire yet.

matt_eng: Can run a smoke + stress sweep. My proposed plan:
- Smoke: single node warmup, 50 qps -> 300 qps ramp over 10m to validate latency curve
- Sustained: steady 300 qps for 30m with 95/99 latency capture
- Burst: 3x ramp to 3k qps over 30s hold for 30s, repeat 3 times with 5m cool-down
- Variant runs: prewarm=off, prewarm=50% nodes, prewarm=100% nodes
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 tokens latency, GPU util, queue depth, cold-start counts, token/sec, error rate

iris_se: Thx. Any recommended batch size / KV cache settings for redwood-13b-quant?

matt_eng: For 13b-quant, recommend dynamic batching up to 8 tokens/batch for thin clients. Enable KV prefix cache at the pod level (helps if many repeated prefixes). For thin single-turns, KV less effective but still useful for system tokens. Use max_seq=512. Also prefer continuous batching with latency SLO 250ms, target per-request max_tokens=256.

sam_sales: @matt_eng can you also give a quick cost delta between hosted vs dedicated for this workload? Exec needs rougher numbers for the quote.

matt_eng: Rough: hosted (shared) -> lower startup but tail latency variance higher. Expect ~1.8x token-cost compared to dedicated because of multiplexing inefficiencies and no reserved GPU. Dedicated reserved nodes -> lower unit cost and more predictable latency. For this profile, if they commit monthly, dedicated reduces token unit cost ~30%. I'll get a per-1M-token estimate after we run.

deploy-bot: Perf job queued: run-1716342901-1 started (smoke). Check logs: https://ci.internal/perf/run-1716342901-1

matt_eng: Smoke done. Results (quick): 50->300 qps ramp ok. Steady 300 qps: p95 = 198ms, p99 = 420ms (a few outliers correlated with small GC spikes). GPU util ~68%. Errors 0.2%.

matt_eng: Burst run (no prewarm): burst to 3k qps -> queueing observed, p95=490ms, p99=1.2s, backend queue depth spiked, lots of cold-start tails. Not meeting SLO.

matt_eng: Burst run (prewarm=50%): p95=230ms, p99=560ms. Better but still some tail. Prewarm=100%: p95=210ms, p99=320ms, cold-starts eliminated. GPU util averaged 85% during burst, token throughput linear-ish.

iris_se: So recommendation: for their SLO p95<250ms under steady and burst, we need dedicated capacity with prewarm policy at >=50% (100% ideal for tight tail). Also configure autoscale burst headroom to add reserve nodes to avoid queueing.

sam_sales: Great. Can you translate that into simple bullets for the customer + a rough cost delta?

matt_eng: Quick customer note:
- Steady 300 qps achievable on dedicated with p95 ~210ms (13b-quant, 120 token prompts).
- Short bursts to 3k qps are possible only with prewarmed capacity; without prewarm p95 can exceed 400ms and p99 >>1s.
- Recommended config: Dedicated pool (reserved), prewarm=100% for burst windows, max_batch=8, max_seq=512, autoscale headroom 30% for sudden surges.

Cost delta (very rough):
- Hosted: ~$0.28 per 1k tokens (estimate) for this workload (higher tail risk).
- Dedicated (reserved monthly): ~$0.19 per 1k tokens equivalent given expected utilization (30% lower unit).
- Add-on: prewarm-reserve nodes increases hourly bill during standby; rough standby = +$2k/day for the footprint required to prewarm 100% for 3k burst (very rough; depends on region).

nora_soleng: I'll convert this into a short one-pager and attach a concise run summary + recommended SLA language. Also will prep the KMS/security questionnaire template to send to Spectra.

sam_sales: Perfect. One more ask: can we capture a short artifact (small CSV) with the latency buckets and GPU util per run? We want to attach to the quote.

matt_eng: Yep — uploading results artifact now. Link: https://s3.internal/redwood-perf/1716342901/sweep-results.csv

iris_se: Next steps: (1) nora to send KMS/security template to customer, (2) sam to share the one-pager + cost delta with execs, (3) eng to produce final per-1M-token estimate after accounting for expected compression/quantization overhead.

sam_sales: Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll draft the external note and loop in Sales AE.

matt_eng: FYI — small follow-up: if they plan to move to multi-turn chat later, re-run recommended (might need higher KV cache benefits and different batch shapes).

nora_soleng: noted. I'll include a 'future chat mode' note in the one-pager.

sam_sales: Closing here. If anyone wants to add quick run screenshots, drop below and I'll add to the customer packet.
